papers_read.title_as_printed: Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis With Brain Structural MRI Using Multiview-Slice Attention and 3D Convolution Neural Network (Chen, Qiao, Zhu, Front. Aging Neurosci. 2022)
Predicting conversion to Alzheimer's disease in individuals with Mild Cognitive Impairment using clinically transferable features (Rye et al., Scientific Reports (2022) 12:15566)

what_each_reports.P-203: The 91.1% accuracy is AD vs CN (trained on ADNI-1, tested on ADNI-2). For pMCI (conversion within 0-36 months) vs sMCI (stable 0-90 months), whole-brain T1 sMRI, trained on ADNI-1 and tested on ADNI-2: ACC 0.801, SEN 0.520, SPE 0.856, AUC 0.789.
what_each_reports.P-212: 678 ADNI MCI across all four phases, each with at least 3 visits and 3 MRIs (321 converted to probable AD at any later visit, 357 stable across all visits); features are demographics, neuropsychological tests (RAVLT, TMT, CFT, GDS, ANART), FreeSurfer total hippocampal volume and binary APOE. Random forest: mean CV accuracy 74.6%, held-out test (n = 139) accuracy 66.2% (SPE 70.3%, SEN 61.5%). Ensemble: CV 74.9%, test 68.3%.

quantity_a: As recorded (91.1): AD vs CN accuracy from T1 sMRI (task T1, not T2). The paper's T2 figure: accuracy 0.801 for pMCI (<= 36 months) vs sMCI from whole-brain T1 images, ADNI-1 -> ADNI-2 cross-phase test.
quantity_b: Accuracy of MCI converting to AD at any later ADNI visit (no fixed horizon) vs MCI stable at all visits, from neuropsychological tests, hippocampal volume, APOE and demographics, internal 21% held-out test.
incompatible_if_same: Not applicable as recorded, because the 91.1 is an AD vs CN result. On the corrected figures (0.801 vs 0.662/0.683), neither paper gives an accuracy interval, and the endpoints and predictors differ, so incompatibility cannot be established.

gates.task: mismatch as recorded: P-203's 91.1 is AD vs CN (T1). After correction both are T2, but P-203 uses a 36-month horizon and P-212 has no fixed horizon (conversion at any subsequent visit).
gates.dataset_family: match: both ADNI (P-212 all phases; P-203 ADNI-1 and ADNI-2); subject overlap is likely.
gates.validation_tier: P-203's MCI result is a train-on-ADNI-1 / test-on-ADNI-2 cross-phase evaluation within the same family; P-212 uses a stratified internal 79/21 holdout.
gates.modality_family: mismatch: P-203 uses T1 sMRI images only; P-212 is predominantly neuropsychological/clinical with one MRI-derived scalar (hippocampal volume) plus APOE.

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible as recorded: claim_a's figure belongs to a different task. After correction the metric types match (accuracy), but the endpoint horizon and predictor set differ.
performance_validity: flag does not apply: no value >= 0.97.
independence: Both draw on ADNI; overlapping MCI subjects are likely. Distinct author groups.
grounds: Claim_a misreads P-203: 91.1% is its AD vs CN accuracy, and its MCI-conversion accuracy is 80.1%.

With claim_a corrected, what remains is a pair of accuracies for different quantities: 36-month conversion from T1 images vs unbounded-horizon conversion from cognitive tests + hippocampal volume + APOE. It is not a disagreement about one quantity.
Neither study claims an ordering the other refutes. P-212 itself calls its accuracy 'modest' and does not compare itself with image-based deep models.

evidence_quotes.quote: our model achieves accuracy values of 91.1 and 80.1% on ADNI-1 for AD diagnosis and mild cognitive impairment (MCI) convention prediction, respectively.

Our top performing RF classification had an average accuracy of 74.6% (mean across 50 cross-validation folds). When the model was evaluated on our unseen test set, the overall classification accuracy was 66.2%.

The other diagnostic group was defined as converters to AD (cAD; n = 321, 47.3%), and included subjects who were diagnosed with MCI at their first study visit, but met the criteria for probable AD on a subsequent assessment
with cognitive function, hippocampal volume and genetic APOE status as features, we obtained a cross-validation classification accuracy of about 70%.

record_defects: claim_a 'P-203: Acc 91.1 on T2' is wrong: 91.1% is AD vs CN; P-203's pMCI vs sMCI accuracy is 80.1% (AUC 0.789).
modality_family 'Neuroimaging' is wrong for P-212, whose features are mainly neuropsychological, with one hippocampal volume and APOE status.

claim_b 'P-212: Acc 66.2' is the random-forest test accuracy; the paper's best test accuracy is the ensemble's 68.3%, and its CV accuracy is 74.6-74.9%. This is not a misreading, but the record does not mention it.
The resolution note's 'bridging evidence' lists scores; it does not bridge anything.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in the two PDFs for this record as written. Setting P-203's corrected 0.801 against P-212 would at most be documented incommensurability, because horizon and predictor set differ; that is not a genuine contradiction.
